scope: Controlled-language empirical evidence for evaluation design; no claim of Korean Protocol efficacy.

sources.title: Controlled Korean for Korean-English MT
sources.methods: 40,000 translation pairs informed rule discovery. Experiment sampled 50 sentences for each of eight error types; only checker-detected suggestions were rewritten. Output translation quality was evaluated, not human task comprehension.
sources.results: Paper reports overall translation accuracy improvement of 4.25%; ambiguous expressions +25%, subject-predicate mismatch +21%, double subject/object +20% in its category table.
sources.limits: Denominator/relative-versus-percentage-point definition of reported improvements, uncertainty intervals and significance are not sufficiently specified. Historical MT system; do not extrapolate to modern LLMs or human reading. Legitimate Korean constructions labeled 'errors' were system difficulties, not universal grammatical defects.
sources.evaluation_implication: Measure ambiguity and semantic role preservation per language/system. Test each rule category independently; do not import English rules wholesale.
sources.verification: Firecrawl PDF 6/6 pages, HTTP200; ACL page metadata verifies 2008 rather than search crawl date.

sources.title: The Comprehensibility of Simplified English in Procedures
sources.methods: SE/non-SE versions of two aircraft-maintenance procedures; outcomes were comprehension, content location and reading-plus-test time. Companion primary author account reports 130 engineering undergraduates, randomized among four documents, 20 two-part questions, 30-minute limit and alpha≤.05.
sources.results: Publisher abstract reports improved comprehension and location for the more complex procedure, and essentially unchanged completion time.
sources.limits: Only two procedures; complexity difference was recognized post hoc in the companion account. Publisher abstract says native-language differences were not statistically tested because cells differed greatly; avoid claiming proven non-native interaction. Full 1995 paper was not obtained.
sources.evaluation_implication: Stratify complexity before testing and separate accuracy, location and time. Questionnaire completion is not operational task success.
sources.verification: Parallel Search publisher abstract plus primary companion paper; full 1995 paper not inspected.

sources.title: Simplified English for Aircraft Workcards
sources.methods: 175 practicing aircraft maintenance technicians in between-subject comprehension testing; 16 workcards crossed language (SE/non-SE), difficulty (easy/difficult) and layout (standard/revised).
sources.results: Publisher abstract reports significant comprehension improvement, especially difficult workcards and non-native speakers; no layout effect.
sources.limits: Abstract lacks effect sizes, confidence intervals and detailed significance tests. Real technicians answered comprehension tests; actual maintenance success was not established. Do not import the 175-person sample as a recommended sample size.
sources.evaluation_implication: Use target readers, include both easy and difficult materials and hold layout constant when testing wording.
sources.verification: Firecrawl rejected for insufficient credits; Parallel publisher extraction fallback.

sources.title: Issues in Conducting Empirical Evaluations of Controlled Languages
sources.methods: Primary authors recount their comprehension and translation experiments and analyze design threats. This overlaps S1995 rather than adding an independent comprehension replication.
sources.results: More complex Procedure A showed comprehension/location gains; Procedure B did not. No significant time difference under a time limit without time pressure. Authors recommend actual procedure performance, representative users and varied complexity.
sources.limits: 130 participants denotes the tested sample in this account, not a confirmed final analysis count in the unavailable 1995 full paper. This account describes native/non-native effects more strongly than the 1995 abstract; retain the abstract's explicit limitation instead of resolving the discrepancy.
sources.evaluation_implication: Separate realistic document tests from minimal rule-pair tests. Predefine success and critical errors; measure actual execution before claiming task benefits.
sources.verification: Firecrawl rejected for insufficient credits; Parallel full-content extraction fallback. 2014-02-11 search metadata is not publication year.

conditions: Korean Protocol edit with recoverable omissions
controls: Same facts, actors, conditions, quantities, negation and obligation strength; blind semantic audit before user testing.
Same layout/font/navigation; randomize or counterbalance conditions so no participant sees multiple versions of the same item.
Stratify easy/complex texts and status/action tasks; include target-domain novices and experienced readers.
primary_outcomes: Correct task completion with predefined critical-error counts.
Correct interpretation of actor, object, scope, precondition and obligation.
secondary_outcomes: Correct-answer or correct-task completion time; report speed/accuracy jointly
rule_ablation: Compare same item with/without subject omission.
Compare same item with/without case particle omission; separately retain meaning-bearing auxiliary particles.
Compare -ㅁ/-음 and finite narrative endings while preserving modality.
Include ambiguous antecedent and scope-loss adversarial items.
analysis: Pre-register outcome definitions and unacceptable semantic-loss threshold; report all conditions and uncertainty intervals.
Use participant and item variability; sample size follows pilot variance and a stated minimum meaningful difference.
LLM judges can screen errors but cannot replace human comprehension or actual task testing.
evaluation_design.claims_allowed_before_testing: External studies motivate the evaluation dimensions; they do not demonstrate Korean Protocol effectiveness.
evaluation_design.no_implementation: No experiment was run and no repository file was modified.
